chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has willed nothing but to make the livelihoods of the believers come from where they do not expect.

key_terms.أَبَى: refused/willed absolutely — expressing divine insistence and decreed will
key_terms.يَحْتَسِبُونَ: they reckon, expect, or calculate — implying human planning and expectation

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about God providing for believers from unexpected sources?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys a divine decree: Allah, in His absolute sovereignty, has arranged for the sustenance (rizq) of the believers to arrive through unexpected channels. This teaching, found in a chapter of al-Kafi devoted to divinely provided livelihood, reassures the faithful that their provision is not contingent solely on their own plans or visible means — God's care for them operates beyond their reckoning. The original audience of Shia Muslims, often living under political pressure, would have understood this as both a theological assertion of divine providence and a practical encouragement to trust in God rather than despair over constrained worldly circumstances.
